items.text: Before comparing numbers, here is what each path actually involves day to day.
A BSc Nursing degree by itself does not make you a Registered Nurse.
The default first job for most BSc Nursing graduates, patient monitoring, medication administration, documentation, and care coordination in a hospital ward.
Manages ventilators, continuous monitoring, and rapid-response patients in intensive care, NICU, or cardiac care units.

blocks.heading: Abroad: Gulf, UK, and US Routes Compared

items.text: International nursing is the most talked-about scope lever for BSc Nursing graduates, but "going abroad" is not one process, it is at least three separate ones, each with its own exam and cost.

Requires DataFlow primary-source verification of your credentials plus a country-specific licensing exam and registration, commonly SCFHS (Saudi Arabia), DHA or HAAD/DOH (Dubai and Abu Dhabi), and QCHP (Qatar).

Requires OET or IELTS (healthcare-specific OET is often more natural for nurses), the NMC computer-based test (CBT), an OSCE clinical assessment, and final registration with the Nursing and Midwifery Council.

blocks.heading: Mistakes That Stall a Nursing Career

items.text: Most stalled nursing careers come from skipped steps and unclear next moves, not from picking the "wrong" specialization.
Most hospitals and most Gulf/UK employers want at least one to two years of general ward or hospital experience before they consider you for ICU charge or an international placement.

blocks.heading: INC, State Councils, and the NNMC Transition

items.text: Parliament passed the National Nursing and Midwifery Commission Act, 2023, which repeals the Indian Nursing Council Act, 1947 and will eventually replace the INC with the National Nursing and Midwifery Commission (NNMC).
The Act also requires every state to set up a State Nursing and Midwifery Commission where one does not already exist.
Implementation is happening in phases, and during this transition the existing legal authority and functions of the INC and current state nursing councils continue to operate.
Complete BSc Nursing and your Indian state council registration.
Pass an English test the NMC accepts, usually IELTS Academic or OET.
Apply to the NMC and pass the computer-based test (CBT), which can be taken in India.
Secure a job offer from a UK employer, then complete the OSCE clinical assessment in the UK.
Receive NMC registration and start at the entry band of the NHS pay structure.
